semantics.note: The proposition preserves the firm forecast about AI broadly and its unspecified horizon. The separate hedged caution about current chatbots does not qualify this forecast.

contract.note: Substantial, established clinical benefits in an important medical field are a fair ordinary reading. The judgment requires interpreting magnitude and validation, but the contract does not demand benefits across all specialties.

evidence.note: This timely peer-reviewed synthesis reports randomized clinical evidence of reduced mortality: RR 0.84, CI 0.75–0.94, NNT 32. These substantial cardiovascular benefits support the forecast despite limitations in blinding and sham controls.

This timely randomized trial found no significant treatment-failure reduction in one LLM-assisted workflow. It limits generalization but does not contradict substantial benefits from other AI applications.

reviews.rationale: The May 6 synthesis meets the early-resolution rule on the contract's ordinary reading: a body of randomized evidence establishes clinically substantial benefits, including reduced mortality, in an important medical field. Reported methodological limitations warrant caution but do not erase that evidence. The unsuccessful LLM trial does not require a mixed verdict because universal success was never claimed.
